# Instructions

Implement a basic reactive system.

Reactive programming is a programming paradigm that focuses on how values are computed in terms of each other to allow a change to one value to automatically propagate to other values, like in a spreadsheet.

Implement a basic reactive system with cells with settable values ("input" cells) and cells with values computed in terms of other cells ("compute" cells).
Implement updates so that when an input value is changed, values propagate to reach a new stable system state.

In addition, compute cells should allow for registering change notification callbacks.
Call a cell’s callbacks when the cell’s value in a new stable state has changed from the previous stable state.

Use the instructions above to complete `react.py`. Keep the existing function and class names: tests you cannot see import them. Use only the Python standard library.

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.')
from react import *
i=InputCell(1); p=ComputeCell([i],lambda v:v[0]+1); t=ComputeCell([i],lambda v:v[0]*10)
o=ComputeCell([p,t],lambda v:v[0]+v[1]); cb=[]; o.add_callback(cb.append)
i.value=3; assert o.value==34 and cb==[34], (o.value,cb)
c=ComputeCell([i],lambda v:1 if v[0]<3 else 2); c2=[]; c.add_callback(c2.append)
i.value=4; assert c2==[]; i.value=1; assert c2==[1]
c.remove_callback(c2.append); c.remove_callback(print); i.value=5; assert c2==[1]
print("ok")
EOF
python /tmp/t.py"}

reasoning.text: I need to handle the React library tests covering setting input values, computing derived cell values, and firing callbacks exactly once per stable change, plus safely removing nonexistent callbacks. I'll implement this with topological propagation: when an input changes, I gather all dependent compute cells, recompute them in order based on a depth level (each compute cell's level is one more than the max level of its inputs), then fire callbacks only for cells whose values actually changed.
